title: Single writer per Hermes home
summary: No two live agent processes write the same Hermes home at the same time.

protected.asset: The state database and configuration of each Hermes home
protected.failure: Concurrent writers corrupt state or silently drop configuration and job changes.

rationale: A Hermes home is designed around one writing process. The moment a second service, sidecar or direct editor writes concurrently, state corruption and lost updates stop being edge cases. Shared deployments need an explicit writer-per-home mapping, and any supervised arrangement is accepted as one crash domain with one writer.

variants.description: Maintain an explicit map of homes to their single writing process, verified against the running process inventory.
Give profiles that cannot share a crash domain their own standalone service on separate data.

verification.method: Compare the live process inventory against the intended writer map: every home has exactly one writing process, and no sidecar starts a second service on the same data.
verification.evidence: Writer-map summary and process-count comparison per home; no process arguments or secrets.

rollback.method: Stop the duplicate writer first, then reconcile any state divergence from backups before resuming.

failure_modes: A debugging sidecar starts a second service on the same data directory.
Direct edits to live stores race the running writer.
A crash-domain split is assumed from profile names without a process check.
